+unreleased
+^^^^^^^^^^
+
+- Fix: Make ``JSONStorage`` writes atomic. The data is now written to a
+  temporary file in the same directory, which then replaces the database
+  file, so the database is no longer corrupted when the process dies or the
+  disk runs full while writing. Temporary files of failed or interrupted
+  writes are removed the next time the database is opened for writing. As a
+  consequence, the directory containing the database file has to be
+  writable.
+

+.. note::
+    ``JSONStorage`` writes atomically: it writes the data to a temporary file
+    in the same directory and then replaces the database file with it. So the
+    database file always contains either the old or the new data, even if the
+    process dies or the disk runs full while writing. If a write fails or the
+    process is killed while writing, its temporary file
+    (``.<file name>.<random>.tinydb.tmp``) is removed the next time the
+    database is opened for writing. This requires
+    the directory containing the database file to be writable. On Windows, a
+    file can't be replaced while another program or ``TinyDB`` instance has it
+    open, so writing fails in that case.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failing_function', ['fsync', 'replace'])
+def test_json_failed_write_keeps_old_data(tmpdir, monkeypatch,
+                                          failing_function):
+    """
+    If a write fails midway (e.g. because the disk is full), the database
+    file has to keep its previous contents
+    """
+    path = str(tmpdir.join('test.db'))
+    old_data = {'_default': {str(i): {'value': 'x' * 50} for i in range(20)}}
+    new_data = {'_default': {}}
+
+    storage = JSONStorage(path)
+    storage.write(old_data)
+
+    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
+        old_contents = handle.read()
+    old_stat = os.stat(path)
+
+    def fail(*args):
+        raise OSError(errno.ENOSPC, 'No space left on device')
+
+    with monkeypatch.context() as m:
+        m.setattr(os, failing_function, fail)
+
+        with pytest.raises(OSError, match='No space left on device'):
+            storage.write(new_data)
+
+    # The database file is exactly as it was...
+    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
+        assert handle.read() == old_contents
+    assert os.path.samestat(os.stat(path), old_stat)
+    assert os.stat(path).st_mtime_ns == old_stat.st_mtime_ns
+    assert storage.read() == old_data
+
+    # ...and the storage can still be used
+    storage.write(new_data)
+    assert storage.read() == new_data
+    storage.close()
+
+    # The temporary file of the failed write is removed when the database is
+    # opened for writing again
+    JSONStorage(path).close()
+    assert os.listdir(str(tmpdir)) == ['test.db']

+    """
+    If the process dies in the middle of a write, the database file has to

+    script = textwrap.dedent('''

+        storage = JSONStorage(sys.argv[1])
+        storage.write({'_default': {'1': {'value': 'old' * 100}}})
+
+        # Kill the process after the new data has been written, but before
+        # the write has finished
